standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of the Picard map for a finite birational morphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Cited as an alternative route to the existence of the glued invertible sheaf; the proof also gives a self-contained direct construction, which is the part counted here.

core_obligations: Set T equal to the union of the pairwise intersections Z_i cap Z_j and observe that, X being reduced, X minus T is the disjoint union of the Z_i minus T, while assumption (3) makes T a discrete subset (proof lines 8012-8016).
For each t in T choose an open U_t containing t and no other point of T, and shrink it so that there are trivializations of the restrictions of the L_i to U_t cap Z_i (proof lines 8017-8021).

Cover each Z_i minus T by open pieces and use the trivializations over the U_t together with the ones on Z_i minus T to produce the transition data for a single invertible sheaf L on X (proof lines 8021-8067).

Carry the sections through the same construction: because the given s_i are nonvanishing at the points of the intersections, the trivializations may be chosen so that the local descriptions of the s_i agree on overlaps, yielding a global section s of L restricting to s_i (proof lines 8000-8004 and 8021-8067).
proof_roadmap: Separate the discrete set of pairwise intersections from the rest of X.
Choose local trivializations on small opens around each intersection point.
Build the cocycle for the glued invertible sheaf from the local pieces.
Track the given sections through the same trivializations to glue them too.
difficulty_reason: The lemma glues invertible sheaves L_i on closed subschemes Z_i covering a reduced scheme X, assuming the pairwise intersections are discrete, and additionally glues sections s_i that are nonvanishing at the points of the intersections. The proof must first note that X minus T is the disjoint union of the Z_i minus T for the discrete set T of pairwise intersections, then choose separating opens U_t around each point of T together with trivializations, cover each Z_i minus T by opens, and build the cocycle data for the glued sheaf (proof lines 8012-8067). The section half of the proof requires keeping track of the chosen trivializations so that the local sections agree on overlaps (proof lines 8021 onwards). H3: the construction of the cocycle and the simultaneous control of the sections is an independent research-level argument, not a routine application of descent.
